leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight members (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Zou) prefer targeted protein degradation as a single prize part, with an identical trio of Crews, Deshaies and Handa. Three of them (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Zou) moved to it after reading the opening ballots, citing breadth of support and mechanistic and structural evidence. Chabes ranked it first from the start. What is shared: the heterobifunctional PROTAC concept plus cereblon identification as the thalidomide target, supported by ternary-complex structures. What is not shared: how much clinical immaturity matters (no approved PROTAC), whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one achievement or two, and whether Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito or Kim should displace a named laureate. Aili, Linke, Somfai and Sparr list B056 only as an alternative, and Aili and Chabes both say they would defer a degradation prize until clinical evidence matures or place it behind another candidate.

Aili and Sparr prefer ionizable lipid nanoparticles, framed as lipid self-assembly and phase behaviour that made siRNA and mRNA medicines possible. They agree on Cullis and Madden but differ on the third name: Aili proposes Anderson (lipidoid screening line), Sparr proposes Hope (Vancouver formulation line). Both explicitly say the decisive-step question (Vancouver encapsulation chemistry versus lipid screening) would decide the choice. Chabes ranks B019 as his fallback after B056; Aqvist's opening ranked it fifth.

A single member, the chair, prefers nanopore sensing of DNA and RNA with Deamer, Akeson and Bayley. The chair's own statement concedes thin breadth of support compared with B056, a contested three-person cut that excludes Branton and Kasianowicz, and an open question whether it is chemistry or instrumentation and genomics.

Somfai alone prefers palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling with Buchwald and Hartwig, citing maturity, clean attribution and bench-level impact. He acknowledges the objection that it is incremental after the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize and has less public reach than the biomedical candidates. Aqvist lists it as an alternative.

areas_of_agreement: B056 is the only shortlisted candidate that all eight members ranked in the opening round, and it appears as a first choice or a stated alternative in every round-1 file except those of Aili, Chabes and Sparr, who also list it as an alternative; every member therefore treats it as a serious option.

Four members (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Zou) propose the same three laureates and a closely matching citation for B056: PROTAC-style induced proximity plus cereblon as the molecular explanation of thalidomide-type glues.

All four B056 supporters explicitly name the absence of an approved PROTAC drug and crowded credit (Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Kim, Ito) as the main reservations, so these are shared concerns and not minority objections.
No member states a specific conflict of interest or recusal need for any shortlisted candidate.
Members broadly prize mechanism that can be stated physically or structurally, independent reproduction, and a result that can be explained in one sentence.
scientific_disputes: Whether targeted protein degradation is new chemistry or mainly pharmacology and chemical biology (raised by Aqvist, Zou, Chabes in their own reservations).

Whether ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a discovery of a chemical principle (pKa tuning, non-bilayer phase behaviour, controlled mixing) or pharmaceutical formulation (raised by Aili and Sparr against their own preference).
Whether nanopore sensing belongs to chemistry or to physics, instrumentation and genomics (raised by the chair).
Whether Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is a distinct advance or an extension of the 2010 C-C cross-coupling logic (raised by Somfai).
Whether the cereblon glue mechanism is established well enough structurally to carry half of a degradation citation (raised by Zou).
attribution_disputes: B056: all four supporters name Crews, Deshaies and Handa, but each flags Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex design) and Sakamoto (first PROTAC paper) as credible omissions; Aqvist notes the opening ballots named Handa as third in six of eight and Ciulli in two. Chabes and Brzezinski question whether PROTAC and cereblon are two lines that a single citation can hold together.

B019: Aili names Cullis, Madden, Anderson and Sparr names Cullis, Madden, Hope. MacLachlan, Langer and Hope or Anderson are left out in either set, and neither member verified patent and priority details.
B017: Deamer, Akeson and Bayley leave out Branton and Kasianowicz, who co-demonstrated translocation in 1996, and the chair asks whether Branton's status affects eligibility.
B016: Somfai limits the names to Buchwald and Hartwig and treats Kosugi and Migita's earlier tin-amide chemistry as a priority question rather than a credit claim.
maturity_disputes: B056: no PROTAC degrader is approved. Aili and Chabes would weigh timing against clinical evidence, and Zou says waiting may be wiser; Aqvist, Brzezinski and Chabes distinguish the approved imid-type glue branch from the unapproved PROTAC branch.

B019: Aili and Sparr treat the record as mature, with decades of independent work and approved products (patisiran, mRNA vaccines), but ask whether the 2023 Medicine prize makes the area feel already honoured.
B017: the chair judges it mature and in wide field use, while noting that it extends to modified bases, RNA and peptides.
B016: Somfai calls recognition mature and arguably overdue after more than 25 years of use.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Brzezinski and Zou disclose a Stockholm University colleague relationship; neither links it to any shortlisted candidate.
Linke, Somfai and Sparr are Lund University colleagues; no member ties this to any shortlisted candidate.

Sparr notes close scientific proximity to B019 (lipid self-assembly) and acknowledges possible overweighting of the phase-behaviour explanation; no personal or institutional tie to any credited name is stated.
Aili notes a shared self-assembly perspective with Sparr and an interest in nanoparticle biomedicine, and states no recusal issue.
questions_for_round2: B056: should the prize part treat PROTACs and molecular glues as one achievement (induced proximity) or two, and if one, which three named individuals hold up on priority between Handa and Ciulli, and does Sakamoto's role in the first PROTAC paper make a trio vulnerable?

B056: is clinical maturity sufficient with no approved PROTAC, given that approved cereblon-directed imid drugs exist, or should recognition wait? Aqvist, Aili, Chabes and Zou take different positions.

B019: was the decisive step the Vancouver encapsulation and ionizable-lipid chemistry (Cullis, Madden, Hope) or the lipidoid library screening line (Anderson, Langer)? This decides between the Aili and Sparr trios.

B019 versus B056: if the committee wants a biomedical prize, which is the more defensible given the 2023 Medicine (mRNA) and 2024 Chemistry (protein) prizes, and could the two be combined as separate prize parts within the three-laureate limit?
B017: does the committee accept a nanopore trio that omits Branton and Kasianowicz, and is nanopore sequencing chemistry rather than instrumentation and genomics?
B016 and B058: Somfai and Aqvist each hold B016 or B058 as a first or alternative position; can either gather support beyond one or two members, and does the 2010 prize reduce the weight of B016?
Can the four B056 supporters and the B019 supporters each state what evidence would move them to the other candidate, so that round 2 can reach a five-vote majority?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows one position with a four-member plurality (B056, identical trio), a two-member position (B019, trio not agreed), and two single-member positions (B017, B016). No position yet reaches the five-vote majority. The central open issues are attribution within B056 and B019, and the timing question for degradation. These are process observations only and carry no ruling.
